summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (about 248 by 242 ft in plan, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise (12 ft per the contractor), rebuilt by Perkins&Will (architect) and Plant Construction (contractor) as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. The DDA terms call for a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease (no executed lease has been found); nearly 90% leased per a Port staff report dated August 7, 2026 (heard as an informational item on August 11, 2026; the minutes call Building 12 the only vertical project so far), with two venture capital firms leasing the whole third floor (The Real Deal reports General Catalyst signed for it).

milestones.text: Built by U.S. Navy personnel as Plate Shop No. 2, the central building of the New Yard on ground leveled from Irish Hill
Listed as a contributing resource of the Union Iron Works Historic District

DDA terms approved: a vertical developer affiliate must take a 66-year lease of Building 12 within a year after completion of the public improvements for Parcel E2, base rent $1/year, participation rent 3.5% of modified gross income from year 31 after TCO, and seek historic tax credits

Phase 1 groundbreaking ceremony for the 28-acre project (the Port release: "celebrated the start of construction on an expansive 28-acre waterfront neighborhood"); it describes Building 12 as a 120,000 sq ft historic structure that Forest City "will be elevating ... nearly nine feet" for sea-level-rise protection, and does not say work on Building 12 itself had begun

Building 15 is lifted in one piece and moved about 200 feet (NBC Bay Area, published October 24, 2018: "workers stripped it down to its frame, lifted it in one piece and wheeled it about 200 feet away Wednesday"). This was the move away from its original site; the Port's June 2025 deck puts the later lift into its permanent position over the newly built 22nd Street somewhere in its 2018-2020 infrastructure window, with no year stated

Building 12 itself lifted (10 ft per the architect, 12 ft per ENR and the contractor) on more than 200 hydraulic jacks over four weeks; the lift was ending in December 2020 (Perkins&Will, December 10, 2020: "This week, the original structure ... will be set down on new precisely constructed columns"). Building 15's own move is the separate October 2018 entry above; no source read dates a Building 15 lift to 2020
Perkins&Will describes the roof-first construction sequence and the lift to address a 100-year sea-level projection
Building 12 receives its temporary certificate of occupancy; The City Canvas: A Paint the Void Retrospective (January 22-30, 2022) draws close to 6,000 attendees

Brookfield reported to have spent $237.4 million on Phase 1, including infrastructure, roads and the Building 12 restoration; the same report (The Real Deal, October 20, 2022) mentions "a recent Oracle NetSuite Open squash tournament hosted in historic Building 12" (the tournament's own date is not given; the milestone date is the report date)
Leases signed in fall 2022 with Standard Deviant Brewing and Breadbelly (in discussions since March 2020)

Seven maker and food tenants announced (Standard Deviant, Breadbelly, Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, and a shared studio for Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis), about 20,000 sq ft in total, leases of three to ten years

Standard Deviant Brewing's taproom opens (SFist, June 6, 2025: "Open as of today (Friday)"; the SF Standard, June 25, 2025, reports it open: "has opened its second taproom"; the Port's June 2025 deck shows it open)

The Real Deal, citing the SF Chronicle, reports General Catalyst signed a 70,000 sq ft office lease for the entire third floor; it also reports Monograph Capital had leased in 2024 (date is the report date, not a stated signing date)

Port staff report for the Commission's Aug 11, 2026 meeting (informational item, no action; report dated Aug 7) says Building 12 is nearly 90% leased, with two venture capital firms leasing the entire third-floor office space

details.text: Developer of Building 12: Port Item 11A (August 2026) names Brookfield Properties as "Developer"; the 2017 Disposition and Development Agreement is with FC Pier 70, LLC, which RDH describes as "an affiliate of Brookfield Properties" and lists, with the Port of San Francisco, as client.

open_questions: Construction cost of the Building 12 rehabilitation itself: not stated anywhere; only the $237.4M Phase 1 total (Oct 2022) and the $150M infrastructure Notice of Completion figure exist.

Whether the 66-year Building 12 lease has been executed, and its date: the DDA sets the trigger, but the Port documents read (Item 11A dated August 7, 2026, and the Commission minutes of July 8, 2025 and August 11, 2026) do not mention a Building 12 lease approval. Item 11A says the Developer "has also signed leases with two venture capital firms for the entire third-floor office space", which does not say whether the Port lease exists. Other Commission agendas from 2018 to 2026 were not searched.
The lift height is given as 9 ft (Port, 2018), 10 ft (Perkins&Will) and 12 ft (ENR, Plant); square footage as 200,000-230,000 depending on source.
The address appears as 1070 Maryland Street (Brookfield, 2026 reports) and 180 Maryland Street (2023 Real Deal report); this record uses 1070.
Sven Ceramics' opening date at 1070 Maryland St is not given by any source found.

Tenants named in Port Item 11A are current as of its Aug 7, 2026 date only; the two third-floor venture capital firms are not named by the Port, and The Real Deal names General Catalyst as taking the entire third floor and Monograph Capital as having leased in 2024, so which firms occupy which space is unresolved.

Standard Deviant's exact opening day: the Chronicle (June 4, 2025) announced Friday, June 6, and SFist's same-day roundup (June 6, 2025) says "Open as of today (Friday)"; the SF Standard (June 25, 2025) reports it open and, on a visit whose date it does not give, "less than two weeks in". No source dated after the opening states the day itself.

No hosted photograph: the four D4D photographs of Building 12 and the D4D Figure 6.6.1/6.6.2 page were removed on 2026-09-29 because the D4D credits its photos to SITELAB urban studio and to Shae Rocco / Forest City (private parties) and grants no reuse licence. No 'now' photograph with a stated open licence was found.

Floor area of Building 12, by source: 118,890 sq ft over two floors historically (NRHP), while ENR calls the original a 60,000-sq-ft warehouse; after adaptive reuse, 230,000 sq ft per the architect; the contractor's page gives both 220,000 sq ft (in its text) and 230,000 sq ft (in its Size field), with 45,000 sq ft of mezzanine and 60,000 sq ft of office; about 200,000 sq ft per the 2026 Real Deal report.

Lift of Building 12, as built: the structure was raised approximately 10 feet per the architect and 12 feet per ENR and the contractor, to sit above 100-year sea-level-rise projections. Planned: the Port's 2018 release said it would be elevated 'nearly nine feet'; that is a plan, not an as-built figure.

Tenants of Building 12, in full: Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) names Standard Deviant Brewing, Breadbelly, Sven Ceramics, Bay Padel, The Plenary Co., Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis, and says two venture capital firms have leased the entire third-floor office space but does not name them. The Real Deal (Jan 2026) reports General Catalyst signed for 70,000 sq ft, taking the entire third floor, and that Monograph Capital 'inked a lease there in 2024'; which firms share the third floor is not stated.
